newsitem.title: UK: Granada holds effective 27 pct of Yorkshire.
newsitem.headline: Granada holds effective 27 pct of Yorkshire.

text.p: Granada's effective stake in Yorkshire Tyne-Tees Television rose to almost 27 percent after the exercise of warrants, Yorkshire said on Wednesday.
A statement from Yorkshire said that Granada itself had a total interest of 18.69 percent of ordinary shares while Allquiet, Granada and Lazard had an interest of 8.27 percent.

Allquiet Trading is a "deadlocked" joint venture company between Lazard and Granada. Deadlocked companies are used to hold stakes which breach media ownership laws pending new UK legislation which takes effect on November 1.
Granada previously had an effective stake of just under 24 percent in neighbour Yorkshire.
The new rules would clear the way for Granada to table a full bid for Yorkshire. But Granada chief executive Charles Allen insisted that a bid was not a foregone conclusion.
"We are still weighing up our options in relation to Yorkshire. Exercising warrants is consistent with whatever course of action we decide to take," he said in a statement.
Yorkshire shares added 5p to 1155p on Wednesday, giving the company a market capitalisation of some 640 million stg. Granada added 5p to 883.5p after earlier hitting a 1996 high of 885p.
